html:
Classic Veracruz was a civilization of the Gulf coast of Mexico, in what is now the state of Veracruz, flourishing from about 100 to 1000 CE. Its greatest city was El Tajín.

Its people were devoted to the ritual ballgame. El Tajín has many ball courts, carved with scenes of players and of sacrifice. Stone yokes, palmas and hachas, carved objects linked to the game, are among its finest art. Its carvers loved interlaced scroll designs. The game itself, played with a solid rubber ball, was shared across Mesoamerica.

The region had been the heartland of the Olmecs a thousand years before. In these centuries it traded with Teotihuacan in the highlands and with the Maya. Later the Totonac people held much of this coast, and it was they who met Hernán Cortés when he landed in 1519.
